candidates.name: R8 Late sniper: at 5 minutes before the start buy every listed bet with EV at least 2.5% (NO GAIN, thin)
candidates.expr:
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'<scratch>/v0701/lib'); from load import load, looks, clv_stats; import numpy as np, pandas as pd
df = load(); L = looks(df); d = df.set_index('id')
L['startsAtMs'] = L.id.map(d.startsAtMs); L['closeFair'] = L.id.map(d.closeFair); L['t_ms'] = L.startsAtMs - L.minToStart*60000   # look time, ms
imp = lambda a: np.where(a<0, -a/(100-a), 100/(100+a))
P = L[L.kind.isin(['c','w'])].sort_values(['id','i']).copy()      # CNO-family PRICE looks: c = the app's CNO list, w = the wide read (same devig; Vigilant's own v looks are separate)
P['cost'] = imp(P.american.astype(float)); P['clv_i'] = P.closeFair/P.cost - 1     # CLV had the bet been bought at THIS look (closeFair/cost - 1)
f = P.groupby('id').head(1).set_index('id')                         # each bet's first c/w look
P['m0'] = P.id.map(f.minToStart)                                     # minutes to the start at the first look
P['age'] = (P.t_ms - P.id.map(f.t_ms))/60000                         # minutes since the first look (known at decision time)
P['improve'] = (P.id.map(f.cost) - P.cost)/P.id.map(f.cost)          # >0 = cheaper than at the first look
W = P[(P.minToStart>=2) & (P.minToStart<=360)]                       # looks inside the 6 h window, pregame with a 2-minute buffer
# every rule below picks ONE look per bet (the first that satisfies it, groupby('id').head(1)) using only that look and earlier looks; CLV/ROI are taken at that look's price. See rules_repro.py for the runnable version.
# for each bet: T = startsAtMs - 5*60000; state at T as in R7; buy at the last c/w price look if listed, <= 7 min old and ev >= 0.025
candidates.rationale: Waiting for the last minutes (small fair drift, the line has settled) is the other timing extreme. 28 bets in 16 games (12/day), 22 closes: CLV +3.72% [+2.81%, +4.59%], but 16 of the 22 closes are Tracker reads taken at about the same minute (circular) and independent closes are +0.58% on 6. The same bets at their first look +2.95%: the paired gain is +0.77 pts. At -15 min 18 bets, +3.81% (14 closes). Inside the 6 h window the time to the start has no slope (-0.05 pts/h, p 0.74).
candidates.baseline_note: the same bets at their first c/w look
candidates.luck_probability: paired sign-flip p = 0.006 on 22 closes/15 games; too few bets to matter: 12 a day, 15% of R1's volume.
candidates.verdict: Not a strategy: tiny volume, no CLV gain over buying at the first qualifying look, higher fill risk (median $33 at the price).

candidates.name: First listed within 6 h AND listed EV at least 2%
candidates.rationale: Inside the 6 h window the listed EV is almost fully kept: CLV climbs monotonically with the EV floor (1%: +2.0%, 1.5%: +2.4%, 2%: +3.0%, 3%: +3.7%, 4%: +4.1%), while beyond 6 h the same floors give +0.3% at 2%. EV >= 2% is the only single add-on to the 6 h window that survives a family-wise test (within-window p=0.020 over 475 rules; excess +1.9 pts over the window's +1.38%); fitted on the first half only it is the top single EV floor in both protocols (excess +1.8 and +2.0 pts) and the second half agrees (+1.9 and +2.0 pts). Nothing else added to the window (shown/hidden, kind, price, books, dollars, sharp verdict, lister) beats noise. The 2.5% variant is rule 3 (the auto-bet's own floor). About 80% of its bets are ones the app's CNO list shows today.
candidates.luck_probability: Chance the true CLV is <= 0 (bootstrap over games): all closes <0.001, close_ok <0.001, independent closes (ESPN/Pinnacle/Novig 3+ trades) <0.001. Chance a rule this good appears among the 5,074 rules tried (cluster sign-flip max-t, 4000 flips, vs the all-closes mean): 0.001 on close_ok, 0.001 on all closes, not testable on independent closes (fewer than 30 of them); naive within-game-day shuffle (iid t-statistic, treats same-game bets as independent): 0.003. Single pre-specified check on the second date half (cluster sign-flip, above that half's mean): loader split p=0.008 (15 closes, 8 games), game-start split p<0.001 (41 closes, 16 games).
candidates.angle: strategy-simple-filters: a few simple first-look filters (1-3 conditions: time to start, listed EV, shown/hidden, kind, league, price band, books behind the fair, dollars available, sharp verdict, lister) on the bets the app lists or could list (all 2,080 logged bets, wide read included). Every rule is evaluated on three yardsticks (all closes, close_ok, independent closes = ESPN/Pinnacle/Novig trades of 3+ with no Tracker close), fitted on the first date half and checked on the second under two protocols, and put through a family-wise permutation test over the whole grid.
candidates.baseline: Universe = all 2,080 logged first-looks (wide read included), 683 with a close in 69 games: CLV +0.19% [-0.33,+0.78] on all closes, +0.19% [-0.32,+0.81] on close_ok (588 closes, 66 games), -0.04% [-0.65,+0.61] on independent closes (360 closes, 57 games); ROI +1.58% on 1,696 settled. Bets first listed more than 6 h out: -0.54% [-1.57,+0.35] (427 closes, 31 games). Every rule below must beat these; the parent universe of each rule is named in baseline_universe.

candidates.name: 6 h trap guard (today 24 h) plus skip when the book page's own edge is 1 point or more under the list's edge
candidates.rationale: Two decision-time signs layered: first listed within 6 h (the repo default; Tj's phone is at 24 h) and, for a bet whose book page was read, the page's own consensus EV (ab_checkEv) not more than 1 point under the EV the list showed (a falling edge between the list and the page). The falling-edge sign works only inside 6 h (WJ within 6 h +3.83 pts [+1.61, +5.49], 10 dropped closes; app universe within 6 h +5.75 [+3.68, +9.13], 5 dropped) and does nothing beyond 6 h; one of the falling-edge half's dropped closes is a -9.3% Tracker close (a bet Tj placed 35 minutes before the start); for the combined rule the worst dropped close is a -30.6% long-lead bet, and without it the gap is still +3.05 pts [+1.09, +5.13]. Cost: drops 36 of 75 bets (48%; 16.0 a day), keeps 17.3 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 13.3 a day instead of 20.8, $63 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $27 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.96 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.85 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $82 a day vs $159.
candidates.verdict: Largest kept CLV (+3.30%) and the clearest gap, same sign on every wider universe and both game-start halves; but (a) only 4 of its kept closes and 10 of its dropped closes are independent closes, and on independent closes the gain is +1.1 pts [-0.9, +3.4] in the app's universe and about 0 on the wider ones (WJ -0.04, 43 vs 52 closes); (b) it keeps only 39 of 75 judged bets; (c) the falling-edge half has only 5 dropped closes inside 6 h in the app's universe.

P['cost'] = imp(P.american.astype(float)); P['clv_i'] = P.closeFair/P.cost - 1     # CLV had the bet been bought at THIS look (closeFair/cost - 1)
f = P.groupby('id').head(1).set_index('id')                         # each bet's first c/w look
P['m0'] = P.id.map(f.minToStart)                                     # minutes to the start at the first look
P['age'] = (P.t_ms - P.id.map(f.t_ms))/60000                         # minutes since the first look (known at decision time)
P['improve'] = (P.id.map(f.cost) - P.cost)/P.id.map(f.cost)          # >0 = cheaper than at the first look
W = P[(P.minToStart>=2) & (P.minToStart<=360)]                       # looks inside the 6 h window, pregame with a 2-minute buffer
# every rule below picks ONE look per bet (the first that satisfies it, groupby('id').head(1)) using only that look and earlier looks; CLV/ROI are taken at that look's price. See rules_repro.py for the runnable version.
R1 = W[W.ev >= 0.025].groupby('id').head(1); R2 = R1[R1.cost < 0.50]
candidates.rationale: At the same listed EV, CLV falls 0.95 pts for every +0.10 of implied probability (SE 0.22, p < 0.001; 378 bets, 59 games); the sign and size hold in both game-day groups (Oct 4: -0.88, Oct 3+5: -0.96). Without any EV gate the in-window entries on plus-money sides closed +1.25% (274 closes/56 games) and the favourites -0.32% (104/38); at cost 0.55 or more -0.96% (36/20). Dog minus favourite +1.57 pts [+1.06 pts, +2.06 pts] on 59 games, same in Oct 4 (+1.54 pts) and Oct 3+5 (+1.43 pts [+0.16 pts, +2.69 pts]). Consistent with the analysts' finding that heavy favourites trap. CAVEAT: against Novig's own last trades alone the cost slope is -0.28 (SE 0.17, p 0.12): the price effect shows against books/consensus closes (ESPN, Tracker), not against Novig's own late price. The 0.50 cut was chosen as 'plus money' before looking at CLV by cut; cuts 0.48/0.52/0.55 on R1 give +2.99%/+2.58%/+2.57% (the effect lives at 0.50-0.55, it is not a cliff).
candidates.baseline_note: R1's favourites (cost >= 0.50) +1.27% on 21 closes/14 games; R2 minus them +1.55 pts [+0.29 pts, +3.22 pts] (bootstrap p 0.008); same bets at first look +1.98%
candidates.luck_probability: Bootstrap p(R2 <= R1 favourites) = 0.008; within-game-day permutation of plus-money vs random R1 events p = 0.060; with the unconditional dog-minus-favourite gap (+1.57 pts, p < 0.001, 59 games) the raw p is about 0.005 for this rule's marginal +1.6 pts and about 0.08 after a Bonferroni-15 haircut: moderately likely real, not proven. candidates.name: R1 EV-gated window entry: buy at the first look inside 6 h of the start where the CNO-family listed EV is at least 2.5%
candidates.expr:
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'<scratch>/v0701/lib'); from load import load, looks, clv_stats; import numpy as np, pandas as pd
df = load(); L = looks(df); d = df.set_index('id')
L['startsAtMs'] = L.id.map(d.startsAtMs); L['closeFair'] = L.id.map(d.closeFair); L['t_ms'] = L.startsAtMs - L.minToStart*60000   # look time, ms
imp = lambda a: np.where(a<0, -a/(100-a), 100/(100+a))
P = L[L.kind.isin(['c','w'])].sort_values(['id','i']).copy()      # CNO-family PRICE looks: c = the app's CNO list, w = the wide read (same devig; Vigilant's own v looks are separate)
P['cost'] = imp(P.american.astype(float)); P['clv_i'] = P.closeFair/P.cost - 1     # CLV had the bet been bought at THIS look (closeFair/cost - 1)
f = P.groupby('id').head(1).set_index('id')                         # each bet's first c/w look
P['m0'] = P.id.map(f.minToStart)                                     # minutes to the start at the first look
P['age'] = (P.t_ms - P.id.map(f.t_ms))/60000                         # minutes since the first look (known at decision time)
P['improve'] = (P.id.map(f.cost) - P.cost)/P.id.map(f.cost)          # >0 = cheaper than at the first look
W = P[(P.minToStart>=2) & (P.minToStart<=360)]                       # looks inside the 6 h window, pregame with a 2-minute buffer
# every rule below picks ONE look per bet (the first that satisfies it, groupby('id').head(1)) using only that look and earlier looks; CLV/ROI are taken at that look's price. See rules_repro.py for the runnable version.
R1 = W[W.ev >= 0.025].groupby('id').head(1)
candidates.rationale: Inside the 6 h window the CLV of a look is almost a straight line in its own listed EV: CLV% = -0.17 + 0.83 x EV% (slope SE 0.16; 378 bets, 59 games; looks weighted 1/bet), and neither time to the start inside the window (-0.05 pts/h, p 0.74) nor how much the price moved since the first look (+0.005 pts per % cheaper, p 0.96) adds anything once EV at the look is known. So the timing rule is: take the FIRST look inside the window at which the EV clears the bar, whether the bet was first seen there or its EV rose into the bar later (requalifiers). Outside the window the same EV does not keep: first look ever with EV >= 2.5% at 6-12 h -0.59% [-3.22%, +2.01%] on 27 closes/11 games, at 12-24 h +1.01% [-0.73%, +2.36%] on 63/20 (RESEARCH.md section 82 found the same 6 h step on Tj's own 176 bets, so the window is replicated, not fitted here). Vs the same bets at their first c/w look (+1.68%) waiting for the EV to qualify adds +0.86 pts [+0.60 pts, +1.11 pts]. HONEST SPLIT BY CLOSE SOURCE: Tracker closes (CNO's own consensus re-read for bets Tj placed, 75 closes) +3.49%; independent closes (Novig 3+ trades, ESPN; 33 closes/23 games) only +0.81% [-0.07%, +2.11%]; bets Tj did not place +0.82% on 41 closes. Close coverage is 63% of R1's bets; re-weighting the closed bets by 1/(closure rate within placed x prop-or-line x game day) gives +2.24% [+1.50%, +3.27%] (raw +2.54%).
candidates.baseline_note: same bets at their first c/w look +1.68%; every c/w bet at first look +0.38% on 571 closes; every OTHER in-window first look (EV < 2.5%) +0.36% on 262 closes (difference +2.19 pts [+1.47 pts, +3.12 pts])
candidates.luck_probability: Game-cluster bootstrap: 0 of 4000 resamples put CLV at or under the all-bets baseline (+0.19%); R1 minus the other in-window entries +2.19 pts [+1.47 pts, +3.12 pts], bootstrap p < 0.001; same-day random picks of 116 in-window entries match it in 0 of 4000 draws (p < 0.00025; ignores same-game correlation, so too optimistic). Replicates in both game-day groups: Oct 4 NFL Sunday +2.14 pts [+1.30 pts, +3.48 pts] (23 games), Oct 3+5 +2.22 pts [+0.90 pts, +3.35 pts] (36 games). After a haircut for ~329 variants in ~15 independent families (Bonferroni 15) the family-wise p is still < 0.01. But the independent-close CLV is +0.81% on 33 closes with one-sided bootstrap p(<=0) = 0.039: about a 1-in-25 chance that the edge against Novig's own last trades is luck, and the Tracker-measured part (+3.5%) is a softer yardstick.
candidates.verdict: Best-supported rule. The app's own CNO list (c looks) is the actionable part: 139 bets (62/day) CLV +2.56% [+1.78%, +3.60%] on 108 closes. ROI -6.73% [-23.03%, +10.60%] on 178 settled bets says nothing yet (needs thousands of bets).

candidates.name: Trap guard 6 h: only bets first listed within 6 h of the start (today 24 h)
candidates.rationale: The only trap sign that is large on the wide samples: first-look lead over 6 h loses to the consensus close (wider universe W: kept +1.41% on 256 closes vs dropped -0.37% on 412, +1.79 pts [+0.93, +2.68], 69 games; within the same game +2.56 [+1.35, +3.81] over 28 games, 82% of games positive). It is the repo's own default (TrapGuard.DEFAULT_EARLY_HOURS = 6). Only 3 of the 106 dropped bets re-enter the 6 h window still listed and passing, so the first-look cut is what the guard really does here. Cost: drops 106 of 182 bets (58%; 47.0 a day), keeps 33.7 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 14.2 a day instead of 20.8, $67 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $29 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.90 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.81 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $158 a day vs $346.
candidates.verdict: Best supported by sample size and by the halves (both game-start halves positive: +2.45 and +1.75 pts). Inside the app's universe the interval touches 0 (+2.12 [-0.58, +5.23], 51 kept vs 69 dropped closes, 20 dropped games). The gap shows against Tracker closes (+3.15 in the app's universe, +2.85 in W) and ESPN (+2.11 in W) but NOT against Novig's own last trades (W -0.15 [-1.7, +1.2]); on all independent closes W +0.89 [-0.11, +1.97]. The dropped bets are not losers in the app's universe (+0.46% [-2.18, +2.79]), so it saves volume more than it saves money.

candidates.name: Wide Novig book: skip a judged bet whose two sides cost 2 cents or more over $1
candidates.rationale: Novig's own book is thin or stale when the price of this side plus the price of the other side comes to 1.02 or more. Those bets lose to the consensus close more often than the rest (the traps analyst's second sign, re-checked here on the app's universe and on wider ones). It needs the other side's price, which is logged only with the book page (judged bets), so it applies to the bets the auto-bet can place. It is a LONG-LEAD sign: inside 6 h it adds nothing (wider judged universe WJ, within 6 h: +0.08 pts [-1.75, +1.48], 30 dropped), and 7 of its 17 dropped bets are the over-6 h ones the 6 h guard would also drop, so it is an alternative to the guard (or a belt-and-braces layer if the guard stays at 24 h), not an addition. Cost: drops 17 of 75 bets (23%; 7.5 a day), keeps 25.7 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 15.1 a day instead of 20.8, $72 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $31 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.61 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.69 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $125 a day vs $159.
